## Episode Thesis

Macro-focused episode with SEB's Robert Bergqvist ahead of a busy week that includes the Riksbank rate decision and April CPI. The shadow board unanimously expects the policy rate to stay at 1.75% for a year, because Swedish inflation is low and falling, helped by the food VAT cut. Bergqvist warned of stagflation risk from oil prices about 50% higher since the Iran war, supply-chain disruption in Asia, weak Swedish employment and Trump's new threat to raise tariffs on European cars and trucks. He also said the stock market has not fully priced in how slowly energy prices come back down.
